text:
sofia: Thinking out loud — propose we introduce 'SLO buckets' for inference: hot (p99 < 50ms), warm (p95 < 200ms), cold (best-effort). This lets us sequence work and map customers to tiers. Thoughts?

jordan: Context? Which customers and what's the revenue impact? :thinking_face:

sofia: Primary ask from Acme + two mid-market customers. Acme needs p99 < 100ms for chat; currently ~180ms. They might move to Dedicated but want a cheaper hosted option too.

eli: Sketched a quick RICE to compare options — numbers are rough but helpful: 
```
Option                           Reach   Impact(1-10)  Confidence  Effort(w)  RICE_score_est
Routing + SLO buckets            500k    6             0.5         4          ~ (6*500k*0.5)/4
Batching + quant for non-hot      400k    5             0.7         3          ~ (5*400k*0.7)/3
Hot-path kernel optimizations     200k    8             0.6         6          ~ (8*200k*0.6)/6
```
Numbers aim to show routing wins on reach/effort tradeoff.

maya: I lean routing + SLO buckets first. Lower effort, immediate customer-facing benefit, and buys time for heavier perf work. Launch criteria idea: mapping logic + telemetry, automated fallback, docs, and measurable cost delta <= 15% for hot traffic.

sam: +1. Also require a canary at 5% traffic, test prompts (edge cases), and regression alerts on p95/p99. We should add an automated rollback if error rate > 1%.

product-bot: Deploy plan created: PR #3472. Canary window: 24h. Alert on p95 increase >10% or error rate >1%.

jordan: One caveat — throughput. Hot-path latency optimizations often reduce batching efficiency -> throughput/cost trade. Need a small QPS vs cost model for each option before final commit.

eli: Quick back-of-envelope: hot optimizations -> GPU utilization +30% -> cost +22% but p99 down by ~55ms. Batching+quant -> cost -18% but median +10ms. Routing keeps hot traffic on low-latency path and sends background to cheaper stacks.

sofia: Proposed sequence: 1) implement routing + SLO buckets + canary 2) deploy batching+quant for non-hot workloads 3) invest in hot-path kernel digs for models with repeatable wins. Does that match product priorities?

maya: Yes. Add launch checklist: customer-facing SLO mapping doc, CS runbook, pricing note, and SLA amendment template for Acme.

jordan: Also need legal signoff for SLA language (Acme). I'll loop in legal.

sam: I'll own the canary runbook and the test harness for latency regressions.

sofia: I'll draft the PRD with acceptance criteria: clear traffic split config, observability dashboards (p50/p95/p99 by bucket), rollback playbook, and cost impact report.

product-bot: Reminder: update changelog and pricing page before GA.

maya: :thumbsup:

jordan: Caveat acknowledged — please include the QPS vs cost model in PRD (even if simple).

sofia: Noted. I'll add a small spreadsheet with assumptions and a sensitivity chart. I'll ping @jordan and @maya when it's ready.

sam: Quick question — do we need model-specific profiles (e.g., Llama-2-Chat vs. small encoder-only) for bucket decisions?

eli: Prefer yes. Different models have different p50/p95 shapes and kernel wins. Routing should be model-aware if we want predictable SLOs.

sofia: Agreement: make bucket mapping support model tags. That can be scoped to optional V1.

product-bot: Thread archived after 48h of inactivity.
